To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Newsgroup Crowd and AuthorLines provide new insights into Usenet activity and can be valuable tools for newsgroup users.
Newsgroup Crowd and AuthorLine interfaces provide a means for users to gain a high level of awareness of the social history of Usenet newsgroup populations.

1) Newsgroup Crowding provides a visual representation of the population of authors and the threads in a newsgroup, 2) AuthorLines provides a visual representation that allows a user to see the posting activity of an author across multiple Usenet newsgroup over a period of time, and 3) Both visualizations provide users with a better understanding of the activity and the population of a newsgroup and the posting activity of a particular author.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of visualizations to support social awareness in conversational spaces.
the exploration of visualizations for the representation and analysis of social information about the authors who participate in Usenet newgroup discussions.
the development of visualizations to help people understand the activity of individuals and groups in large-scale conversational spaces.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
these interfaces can help users to understand and navigate Usenet.
this is a good paper, and that the authors are to be commended on a job well done.

the newsgroup crowds and author lines visualizations are useful tools for understanding the activity of individuals and populations in Usenet newgroups and for selecting and evaluating newsgroup content.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the social history of a population is an important aspect of the social context of a conversational space and that visualizations that convey this information are useful for understanding and evaluating conversational cyberspace.
the visualizations of the social history of the newsgroup populations and individual authors are useful for developing a high-level awareness of their activity and population.
we have designed two new interfaces for exploring the activity of Usenet newsgroup populations and individuals.
The main takeaway from our work is that
social awareness of the population of participants is a valuable component in the design of interfaces for conversational cyberspace.
there are many opportunities for new visual interfaces that can help people make sense of the social aspects of online conversations.
visualizing social histories of populations of individuals can be a useful tool to support awareness of conversational spaces.
